segments.title: Compatibility
segments.description: Degree to which a product, system or component can exchange information with other products, systems or components.
segments.label: Segment 1

segments.title: FAIRness
segments.description: FAIRness refers to the degree to which research software adheres to the FAIR principles.
segments.label: Segment 2

segments.title: Flexibility
segments.description: Degree to which a product can be adapted to changes in its requirements, contexts of use or system environment.
segments.label: Segment 3

segments.title: Functional Suitability
segments.description: The degree to which a product or system provides functions that meet stated and implied needs.
segments.label: Segment 4

segments.title: Interaction Capability
segments.description: The degree to which a product or system supports users in performing their tasks.
segments.label: Segment 5

segments.title: Maintainability
segments.description: The degree of effectiveness and efficiency with which a product can be modified.
segments.label: Segment 6

segments.title: Performance Efficiency
segments.description: The degree to which a product performs its functions within specified parameters.
segments.label: Segment 7

segments.title: Reliability
segments.description: Degree to which a system performs specified functions under specified conditions.
segments.label: Segment 8

segments.title: Safety
segments.description: The degree to which a product avoids a state in which human life, health, or environment is endangered.
segments.label: Segment 9

segments.title: Security
segments.description: Degree to which a product protects information and data.
segments.label: Segment 10

segments.title: Sustainability
segments.description: The capacity of the software to endure.
segments.label: Segment 11
